entries.definition: Resources are limited relative to the wants people seek to satisfy.
The value of the next-best alternative forgone when a choice is made.
Produced resources used to make other goods and services; financial capital must be distinguished when that sense is intended.
Natural resources used in production.
Human physical and mental effort used in production.
Organising productive resources and bearing the risk of business decisions.
Concentrating productive activity on a narrower range of tasks or products.
Splitting a production process into tasks performed by different workers or groups.
An economy in which market prices and private decisions play the main role in allocating resources.
An economy in which government planning directs the main resource-allocation decisions.
An economy combining market allocation with government ownership, provision or intervention.
Economic activity owned and controlled by private individuals or organisations.
Economic activity owned or controlled by government.
An individual who owns an unincorporated business and bears its business obligations personally.
A business owned jointly by partners; avoid unsupported universal legal membership limits.
An incorporated business whose shares are not offered freely to the general public.
A company permitted to offer shares to the public; this does not mean government ownership.
A business with productive operations in more than one country; this describes geographic operations rather than a universal legal form.
An organisation owned by members to pursue their common economic interests.
An incorporated business with member ownership; describe the syllabus-level distinction without inventing current statutory thresholds.
An organisation established for public purposes and owned or controlled by the state.
An organisation representing workers in dealings with employers.
An organisation representing the interests of employers, often within an industry.
Negotiation between representatives of workers and employers over matters such as pay and working conditions.
An asset generally accepted as a means of payment and used to express value.
Uniformity of units of the same denomination, rather than equality of value across different denominations.
An institution responsible for currency, monetary arrangements and banking-system functions such as acting as banker to government and banks.
A bank providing deposit, payment and lending services to customers.
An organised market for trading shares and other financial securities.
The value of one currency expressed in terms of another currency.
A fall in a currency's value relative to other currencies under market determination.
A rise in a currency's value relative to other currencies under market determination.
An arrangement through which buyers and sellers interact to exchange a product and determine its price.
The quantities buyers are willing and able to buy at different prices over a stated period, other relevant conditions unchanged.
The quantities producers are willing and able to offer at different prices over a stated period, other relevant conditions unchanged.
A price and quantity at which quantity demanded equals quantity supplied.
The responsiveness of quantity demanded to a price change, measured by percentage change in quantity demanded divided by percentage change in price.
The responsiveness of quantity supplied to a price change, measured by percentage change in quantity supplied divided by percentage change in price.
Demand for goods used together, such as complementary products.
A good that can serve as an alternative to another good in meeting a similar want.
A market model with many small price-taking firms selling homogeneous products, with entry and exit and relevant information available.
A market with a single seller of the relevant product; define the relevant market before making the claim.
Income available for spending and saving after relevant taxes and deductions.
Income adjusted for the price level, indicating purchasing power.
The part of a factor's reward above the minimum needed to keep it in its current use.
The minimum reward needed to retain a factor in its current use.
The creation of goods and services or addition of value through productive activity.
Output per unit of input over a specified period.
The sum of fixed and variable costs at a specified output.
Total cost divided by output.
A cost that does not vary with output over the relevant period and capacity range; its level can change over time.
A cost that varies with the level of output over the relevant period.
The amount received from sales; for a single product at one price, price multiplied by quantity sold.
Total revenue divided by quantity sold.
The additional revenue from selling one more unit.
The additional cost of producing one more unit.
Total revenue minus total cost over the stated period.
Choosing the feasible output or decision giving the highest profit; the relevant marginal-cost/marginal-revenue condition needs the appropriate maximising context.
Reductions in long-run average cost as the scale of production increases.
Increases in long-run average cost as the scale of production increases.
Use of government spending and taxation to pursue economic objectives.
Use of monetary and credit conditions, including interest rates and money supply, to pursue economic objectives.
Government expenditure exceeds government revenue over the stated period.
Government revenue exceeds government expenditure over the stated period.
A tax whose rate remains a constant proportion of the relevant income or tax base.
A tax for which the proportion of income paid in tax rises as income rises.
A tax for which the proportion of income paid in tax falls as income rises.
A sustained increase in the general price level, reducing the purchasing power of money.
An index tracking changes in the cost of a weighted basket of consumer goods and services relative to a base period.
People of working age who are willing and able to work and seeking work but unable to find it, subject to the stated measurement convention.
The value of final goods and services produced within an economy over a stated period.
Domestic product adjusted for net primary income from abroad in the syllabus's national-product terminology.
Income generated by the factors of production of an economy over a stated period; state the measurement basis when comparing totals.
An increase in real output over time; distinguish total growth from growth per person.
The value of goods exports minus the value of goods imports over a stated period.
A record of economic transactions between residents of an economy and the rest of the world over a stated period.
Ability to produce more output with the same resources, or the same output with fewer resources.
Ability to produce a good at a lower opportunity cost than another producer.
Immigration minus emigration over a stated period; a rate additionally requires a stated population denominator.
Births minus deaths over a stated period, excluding migration.
The average number of years a person is expected to live under the stated mortality conditions.
Private cost plus external cost.
An uncompensated cost of an activity borne by a third party.
Private benefit plus external benefit.
A good whose consumption is non-rival and non-excludable in the relevant setting.
A good judged beneficial to users and society that may be underconsumed when decisions are left entirely to the market.
A good available without sacrificing scarce resources at the relevant margin; a zero monetary price does not establish this.
In the productive sense, expenditure adding to capital goods; distinguish financial purchases or deposits when the context uses that sense.
A tax on imports.
A physical or quantity limit on the specified imports, production or extraction.
Government financial assistance that supports an activity, such as reducing producers' costs.
Comparison of the valued alternatives forgone by different feasible decisions, using a consistent time horizon and relevant constraints.
